messages:
okta-bot: ALERT: unusual MFA push volume detected for org 'redwood-prod' (high severity). 45 distinct users received 100+ push prompts in last 10m. See /alerts/1840126789.

mia: seeing same. users mostly in EU + one in US-west but with very short delta between logins (~2m). possible automation trying to brute-force approval?

omar: pulling raw auth logs now. initial look: repeated PUSH events from several ASNs (AS64512, AS12345) hitting our Okta endpoints. IP sample: 198.51.100.23, 203.0.113.8 (redacted).

ashley: tagging @oncall-sre and @product-security. Are any admin consoles showing suspicious activity?

jules: no admin console writes so far. looks like user-level push spam, not admin takeover. I can run bulk revoke of refresh tokens for impacted users. Recommend block-before-revoke to stop more prompts.

mia: agreed. immediate actions: 1) block IPs at WAF 2) add temporary rate-limit rule on /api/v1/authorize 3) revoke refresh tokens for affected users 4) put Okta sign-on policy to require re-auth for high-risk geos. I'll coordinate.

omar: WAF rule pushed: `deny ip 198.51.100.0/24` + `deny ip 203.0.113.0/24` (applied to prod-egress). Also added a per-user push throttle: 5 pushes / 10m.

jules: running revoke script now. curl snippet: ```bash
for u in $(cat impacted_users.txt); do
  curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: SSWS $OKTA_TOKEN' 
  "https://redwood.okta.com/api/v1/users/$u/lifecycle/expire_password"
done
```
(revokes and forces re-auth on next connect).

ashley: @mia can you check KMS/admin audit logs for any key usage or role changes in the same window? want to ensure this isn't an escalation attempt.

mia: checked Cloud KMS logs -> no key encrypt/decrypt or IAM policy changes in the window. IAM last admin action was 12hrs earlier. Good. Also checked console access logs -> no admin sign-ins.

sre-bot: Deploy lock engaged: disables config pushes to auth-related rules until incident cleared.

omar: Okta fine-grained audit exported to s3://redwood-security/incidents/1840126789-auth-logs.json.gz (sensitive fields redacted).

jules: created incident PD-8421, linked logs, and set severity P2. Notifying legal and support for customer comms draft.

ashley: action items list: - finalize user revoke list (jules) - update Okta sign-on policy (mia) - implement permanent per-user push rate limit and anomaly detector (omar) - check RBAC for console admin-only via hardware 2FA group (ashley) - postmortem in 72h (jules to own).

mia: quick mitigation note: we added a temporary RBAC constraint on admin API keys: only `admin-2fa` group can call. This is a short-lived change until we validate KMS/HSM audit trail.

omar: monitoring: set up a CloudWatch alarm for >10 push cancellations/min and a SIEM rule to alert on repeated okta.challenge.cancel events.

jules: support comms draft ready, asking for approvals: "We observed an automated MFA push campaign targeting user devices; no admin consoles were accessed and no KMS key operations occurred. Affected users were forced to re-auth. We're continuing monitoring."

ashley: approve. send to legal for final language. Also schedule rotation window for any API keys used to manage Okta integrations if we see any suspicious lifetime extensions.

mia: incident status -> contained. WAF rules + per-user throttle + token revokes done. Monitoring in elevated state for 24h.

jules: I'll file follow-up tickets: 1) permanent push-rate detector + blocklist automation, 2) RBAC review for admin keys, 3) audit-log retention increase + KMS key-usage alerting.

omar: leaving note for postmortem: consider adding HSM-backed signed challenge for push prompts to reduce automated acceptance attempts.

sre-bot: Incident PD-8421 updated to RESOLVED (containment) — follow-ups scheduled. :white_check_mark:
